newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht, interbank rates ease late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht, interbank rates ease late.

text.p: The Thai baht eased against the dollar late on Tuesday on sustained dollar buying and continued absence of positive news for the Thai economy, dealers said.

The baht weakened marginally to 30.900/31.000 to the dollar in the local market during late afternoon trade against 30.800/30.900 in the morning. It also eased offshore to 30.450/30.950 from 30.20/30.40 in the morning.
The Thai market was closed on Monday for a Buddhist featival holiday.

"We saw follow-up buying from Friday and some commercial demand for dollar. Most people still hung on to the dollar amid the absence of positive news. The broader market is waiting for non-performing loan figures of financial institutions due later this month," a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Dealers said trading was thinned by the market focus on the rupiah and ringgit which, they said, dampened sentiment for all south east Asian currencies.
The Bank of Thailand on Tuesday announced the baht's weighted average interbank exchange rate of 30.370 per dollar, against 30.127 on Friday.
The overnight interbank rate eased to 15-16 percent shortly before close from 16-18 percent in the morning after most banks met their fortnightly reserve requirements.

"The baht interbank market looks pretty liquid this week with some foreign funds coming to the stock market while currency players may need to accumulate long baht positions for their mid-August needs," a treasury bank official said.
"The overnight rate should not stay too high this week," she said.
